metadata.hardware_requirements: NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU, Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores) ("on a computing server with NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores)")

nodes_source.source_quote: A series of simulation experiments based on real-world traffic data are conducted to evaluate the proposed approach.
nodes_source.description: Traffic volumes and behavioral calibration data from the freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao through a tunnel in Shandong, China, used for microscopic simulation.
nodes_source.size_estimate: 10-min traffic volumes from 7:50 a.m. to 9:00 a.m.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Statement on page 12 explicitly notes that data is available from the corresponding author upon request.

nodes_process.node_name: Vehicle Extraction and State Matrix Representation
nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations are extracted from the traffic video frames and are reformed as position matrices.
nodes_process.description: Extracts vehicle coordinates (xi, yi) from raw video frames to form position matrices mt. Stacks N consecutive matrices to represent traffic dynamics in state st.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, generic extraction tool unamed but procedure and dimensions fully specified.

nodes_process.source_quote: The Q-network in Mnih et al. [30] is revised as Figure 7, which consists of three convolutional neural network (CNN) layers and one full connection (FC) layer for each output layer.
nodes_process.description: Implements a DRL architecture with three CNN layers and a multitask learning head for Q-value estimation and traffic state prediction (speed and queue length).
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all architecture parameters detailed in Figure 7.

nodes_process.source_quote: The training problem can be viewed as the regression problem with the loss function defined by the following: L(wi) = L1(wi) + lambda*L2(wi).
nodes_process.description: Trains the agent using Adam optimizer, experience replay, and a target network. Optimization objective balances discounted cumulative reward with speed/queue prediction accuracy.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all training hyperparameters and optimization algorithms specified in Table 1.

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator [31].
nodes_process.description: Runs 20 simulation experiments in SUMO across three scenarios: no control, PI-ALINEA baseline, and the proposed DRL method. Measures travel times, speeds, and queue lengths.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, SUMO simulator named but its specific version and precise config files are missing.

nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data.
nodes_process.description: Divides the control area into 8 subareas and removes information from each subarea sequentially to test DRL controller sensitivity and robustness.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, logic of subarea removal explained but division coordinates for 8 zones are illustrative only.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 6 presents the 10-min traffic volumes from 7:50 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. in the mainline and at the on-ramp.
nodes_sink.description: Bar chart showing input traffic volume profiles for simulation experiments in the mainline and on-ramp across time intervals.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Empirical data is visualized clearly but raw numerical source files are not linked.

nodes_sink.source_quote: The training process, presented in Figure 8, can be finished in less than 24 hours on a computing server... episode reward and mean travel time are both converged in 400,000 training frames.
nodes_sink.description: Convergence curves showing (a) cumulative episode reward and (b) mean mainline travel time across 1 million training frames.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Training logic and hyperparameters in Table 1 support replication; specific random seeds are unstated.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 9 presents the Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) of the travel times in the mainline for three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Distribution of mainline travel times over time for No Control, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clear procedure within SUMO simulator; specific demand peaks described and results follow logically.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Table 2 presents mean vehicle travel times in 20 simulation experiments. It is found that the performance of the PI-ALINEA method is not always better than that of the no-control scenario.
nodes_sink.description: Quantitative comparison of mean travel times (s) for 20 simulation runs comparing three control methods.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Detailed per-experiment results provided for multiple baselines using stated parameters.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 10 presents the temporal-spatial distribution of the mean speeds along the mainline.
nodes_sink.description: Spatiotemporal speed heatmaps for No control, PI-ALINEA, and DRL, visualizing the extent and duration of traffic congestion.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Visual outcome derived directly from simulation data using standard speed-density-time plots.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 11 presents the Q1, Q2, and Q3 of the queue lengths at the on-ramp in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Time-varying quartiles of vehicle queue lengths (m) on the on-ramp for three scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Outcome measures defined and derived from simulated environment outputs.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 12 presents the mean queue lengths at the on ramp and the red ratios ... in each simulation for the two ramp metering methods.
nodes_sink.description: Correlation plot between signal red-time ratio and mean queue length for PI-ALINEA versus DRL methods.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Procedure stated but exact derivation of red ratio in PI-ALINEA tuning lacks minor details.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 13 presents the queue length at the on-ramp and the occupancy downstream of the merging area for the two ramp metering methods.
nodes_sink.description: Dual-axis time series plots showing the correlation (rho values provided) between occupancy and queue length for two methods.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Correlation metrics clearly defined and results plausibly follow from simulation trajectories.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 14: Downstream volume in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Box plots of traffic volume (veh/h) downstream of the merging area at 5-minute intervals for three scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Volume measurement locations stated; results consistent with capacity drop analysis.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 16 presents the box plot of travel time when the information of different subareas is removed.
nodes_sink.description: Sensitivity analysis results showing mean travel times across 8 perturbed input configurations (omitted video subareas).
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Division of subareas clearly illustrated in Figure 15, procedure for perturbation specified.
